reviews.title: This is life-changing
reviews.text: I regularly do EMDR and brain mapping with my therapist. This on the other hand is something I can do several times a day and it has helped me in so many instances. For example, I own my own business and I’m extremely stressed out. I have to force myself to sit on my couch to scroll aimlessly through a social media as a “break” this never released my anxiety and made me more tired. I’ve been only using it for a few days, but during these times I’ve experienced; crying, euphoria, huge body sensations, like I am floating out of my body, including severe nose flaring. I don’t know what that’s about. But the best part is, when I’m done I feel alive in my brain feels clear. Nothing ever this as this app has and I thank you guys so much.

reviews.title: These reviews have to be bought
reviews.text:
Cool idea, but this all seems like something I could’ve thrown together myself with Claude. I own the nova, and the lowest setting isn’t low enough. It’s certainly not good for sleep. If you’ve actually done psychedelics, then these ‘visuals’ will not be what you’re expecting/hoping for. 

The music has zero thoughtfulness put into it. It’s your standard padded chords with some synth wave leads layered on top and then looped forever at low fidelity.

The voiceovers for guided meditation are AI (ew) and are brief. And also poor audio quality. 

Listen, again, cool idea, but how dare you sell a $150 device and then force your users to pay for a $70/yr subscription (or whatever the price is now) just to access more than 4 pieces of content. I pay for the subscription and compared to Calm, Mesmerise, Endel, I’m pretty disappointed in the quality of content and massive overpromise Lumenate has made. 

This is just fancy marketing with a vibe coded product. Unfortunately I think we can expect to see a lot more of this caliber of stuff in the world coming soon. And then they’ll all buy reviews like Lumenate has done which will trick the general population into thinking it’s good. C’est la vie.

Perhaps before you have users fill out all that info, you tell them upfront that you need to subscribe. Sure, you have a free trial but I'm not signing up for that. I always forget to cancel before the trial is up. Thanks for wasting my time and making me fill out all this info and go through the tips and tutorial only to find in the end that I had to subscribe to even test it. Deleted the app and will not ever reinstall.

reviews.title: The fix I have been looking for so long!
reviews.text: Got an ad on Youtube with Rhett and Link. I thought it was Ai so I looked it up and sure enough it was real, I watched the video as they went through the spinning column, the app and the weird iPod thing and i was very skeptical. As much as I hate subscription services, I can firmly say that this is 100% worth it for me. I have taken a THC gummy once a month to help with my depression and anxiety revolving past mistakes that keep me up at night crying, and while this does not give you the physical sensation, the mental sensation was tied neck and neck in terms of calming me down. I have officially, as of this moment, quit taking THC and I am going using this app every night. I am very interested on purchasing the Nova Mask they sell. If you’re skeptical, try the free week. I never write reviews for anything I purchase, but nothing in my life has made me feel so strongly to voice support for a product.
